angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 81,189,581 km at 215.98 pc = 5.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: distance 215.983 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.06), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 215.983 +/- 12.959 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 5.5124 +/- 0.1415 mas (same row, RUWE 2.15), 38.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 116.702 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: radius 116.702 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 2193.28 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.091) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 81,189,581 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3659 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: effective temperature 3659 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.133) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: effective temperature 3659 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.133) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
